relatedSnapshot.title: ColdMailReseller pre-warmed inboxes stuck in Error: reconnect sends mailboxId=undefined ("Mailbox not found")
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Pre-warmed mailboxes provisioned through ColdMailReseller get stuck in an Error state and cannot send, because no reconnect path resolves a mailbox id the provider will accept.

## Problem

When a ColdMailReseller pre-warmed inbox disconnects or needs reconnecting, the account-error reconnect flow fires with `mailboxId: providerId ?? undefined`. These inboxes have `mail_inbox.provider_id = NULL`, so the provider receives `mailboxId=undefined` and the OAuth connect returns "Mailbox not found", leaving the inbox permanently in Error.

## Root cause

`apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/campaign/workspaces/process-account-error-reconnect.ts` invokes `processConnectOAuth` with `mailboxId: inboxLookup.providerId ?? undefined`. `processConnectOAuth` (`process-connect-oauth.ts`, `connect-mailbox-oauth` step) forwards that `mailboxId` to ColdMailReseller `POST /mailboxes/oauth` via `apps/web/lib/mail/providers/coldmailreseller/client.ts#connectMailboxOAuth`, which rejects it with "Mailbox not found". The inboxes have `mail_inbox.provider_id = NULL`, so the id is never resolved. The reconcile cron (`reconcile-domain-orders-cron.ts`) already looks up the mailbox from ColdMailReseller and passes `mailbox.id` correctly, so the resolution pattern exists.

The failing invariant is one gap across every entry point: no reconnect path resolves the mailbox id from ColdMailReseller before calling the provider. The webhook path forwards the stored `mail_inbox.provider_id`; the customer Reconnect action (`email-accounts.ts`, `triggerOAuthReconnect`) and the admin reconnect (`admin-domain-orders.ts`) both send `mailboxId: undefined`; `processConnectOAuth` never re-resolves. An inbox carrying a named but no-longer-valid id fails identically to one with a NULL id, which is why both counts below sit in this one class.

## Blast radius

5,762 inboxes across 444 organizations carry a `connection_error` containing "Mailbox not found" (query: `SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT organization_id) FROM mail_inbox WHERE connection_error ILIKE '%Mailbox not found%'`, counted 2026-09-24: 5,762 inboxes / 444 organizations, and 7,071 reconnect sessions across 461 organizations failed the same way in the 30 days to 2026-09-24; was 5,763 / 445 on 2026-09-23, 5,660 / 439 on 2026-09-22, 4,364 / 323 on 2026-09-10 and 294 / 39 on 2026-08-28). None of the 5,762 is connected now. 2,391 of them carry the exact `mailboxId=undefined` signature (and all of those have `provider_id IS NULL`); the larger 3,371 carry a named mailbox id and fail the same way. Named-id rows arrive in platform waves (2026-09-04 to 09-06 roughly 2,118 rows across 95+ organizations; 2026-09-19 to 09-20 roughly 1,148 rows across 103 organizations), so the shape is systematic rather than org-specific. A further 2,872 connected pre-warmed inboxes across 228 organizations sit at `provider_id IS NULL` and would fail the same way on their next reconnect.

## Proposed fix

Resolve the provider mailbox id before reconnecting: look up the mailbox from ColdMailReseller (as the reconcile cron already does) instead of passing `provider_id` or `undefined`, and backfill `provider_id` for the affected inboxes so they reconnect successfully.

## Done when

* No reconnect path hands ColdMailReseller an unresolved id: the webhook path stops forwarding the stored `provider_id` unresolved, the customer Reconnect and admin reconnect stop sending `undefined`, and both shapes (NULL `provider_id` and stale named id) reconnect successfully.
* The stuck inboxes are recovered or re-provisioned and resume sending.
* Provider accounts with no local `mail_inbox` row are covered too: Reconnect refuses them outright (`email-accounts.ts#triggerOAuthReconnect` throws PRECONDITION_FAILED "Only managed inboxes can be reconnected.") while their inbox entitlements are still consumed, so the backfill and re-provision step must create or link the missing rows, not only repair a NULL or stale `provider_id`.

## Reports

* ENG-13156
* ENG-13255
* ENG-13511
* ENG-14104
* ENG-14131
* ENG-14197 Customer report: all 15 pre-warmed inboxes stuck in Error; Reconnect returns Mailbox not found; campaigns cannot send
* ENG-14201 Customer report: 15 of 36 pre-warmed inboxes stuck in Error; Reconnect returns Mailbox not found and never clears the inbox

relatedSnapshot.title: Customer report: 9 of 9 pre-warmed inboxes stuck in Error for over a week, customer Reconnect still returns "Mailbox not found"
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Source

Intercom conversation: <url:app.intercom.com>

## Bounded conversation context

Customer wrote on 2026-10-01: "HI guys, my inboxes are still burned. Can I escalate please to get solved asap thanks". The conversation link points at Cold Email Agent > Email Accounts for workspace "<workspace-slug>". Asked twice for a human ("human", "no i need it looked at by a human please") and said the state had persisted "been this way for over a week now". The front-line agent replied 2026-10-02 01:15Z: "Hi Name 2. Let me look into this and I will get back to you". Product area named on the conversation: Email accounts & domains. No financial remedy requested.

* Repeat of the same customer's earlier report (ENG-14130, "Name 2 - inboxes burned", created 2026-09-22), which is already Duplicate of master ENG-13178.

## Testable claim

In workspace "Name 2's Workspace" (organization <uuid>), all 9 platform-managed pre-warmed inboxes sit at status=error / connected=false and cannot be restored by the documented customer action (Cold Email Agent > Email Accounts > Reconnect): the reconnect runs but the provider answers "Mailbox not found", so the inboxes stay in Error and the customer cannot send, which has persisted since at least 2026-09-19.

## Current evidence

* PlanetScale (counted 2026-10-02): all 9 mail_inbox rows in the pinned org are mailbox_type='prewarmed', status='error', connected=false. Five carry connection_error "Mailbox OAuth connection threw an exception: Mailbox not found. Context: mailboxId=<stored provider id>, email=..."; four carry "Disconnected via Company One account_error webhook".
* PlanetScale cea_oauth_sessions: 16 failed sessions for this org, the newest on 2026-10-02 01:19Z, all erroring with "Mailbox not found". Two of the 2026-10-01 sessions carry the exact "mailboxId=undefined" signature (<email>, <email>), which is the in-product Reconnect button's payload.
* Provider (Company One) subworkspace "Name 2's Workspace" (<uuid>): all sending accounts report status -1 (connection error), warmup score 100.
* Code (Acquisity/Acquisity at bd59246c7f993b07fab3c1ed967cedb1ea6af4d8): apps/web/trpc/routers/outreach/email-accounts.ts#triggerOAuthReconnect sends the connect-oauth event with mailboxId: undefined, orderId: undefined, domain: undefined; apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/campaign/workspaces/process-account-error-reconnect.ts#processAccountErrorReconnect invokes processConnectOAuth with mailboxId: inboxLookup.providerId ?? undefined (line 209); apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/campaign/workspaces/process-connect-oauth.ts#connect-mailbox-oauth forwards it to ColdMailReseller connectMailboxOAuth, which rejects it.
* Help centre (apps/web/content/docs/cold-email-agent/email-accounts/dfy-warmup-and-reconnect-errors.mdx) documents Reconnect as the fix and tells the customer to escalate to support if Error persists after 48 hours; here that documented step itself fails.

## Relationship

Same root cause as master ENG-13178 (ColdMailReseller pre-warmed inboxes stuck in Error: reconnect sends mailboxId=undefined). This report should be attached as a child of ENG-13178, not treated as a fresh root cause.

relatedSnapshot.title: Reconcile retry gate treats a failed mailbox OAuth session as in flight for 48h, so pre-warmed inbox retries stall
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

A mailbox whose OAuth connect to the mail provider fails is retried at a two-day cadence instead of every 30 minutes, because the provisioning reconcile loop counts the failure's own OAuth session as work still in flight. Pre-warmed inboxes stay in Error and their orders sit in `requires_attention`, so customers who paid for inboxes cannot send for days and the UI eventually reports the retry budget as exhausted.

## Problem

A workspace buys pre-warmed inboxes. The domains provision, the mailbox rows are created, and then nothing completes: Email Accounts shows the mailboxes in Error, the order banner says provisioning requires attention, and later "N mailboxes could not be retried / Retry budget exhausted. Contact support to re-run these exports." No customer action changes it; Reconnect re-enters the same failing path.

## Root cause

`recordConnectionFailure` (`apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/campaign/workspaces/oauth-connection-failure.ts`) defaults to `sessionStatus: 'failed'` and marks the newest `cea_oauth_sessions` row for the mailbox+order failed. Both connect-failure shapes reach it from `processConnectOAuth`'s `connect-mailbox-oauth` step (`apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/campaign/workspaces/process-connect-oauth.ts`): a `status === 'failed'` result and a thrown `ApiClientError` (for example the provider's HTTP 429 "Rate limit exceeded, please try again later.").

`reconcileDomainOrdersCron` (`apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/billing/reconcile-domain-orders-cron.ts`, `find-orders-requiring-attention` loop, skip predicate around l.1168–1185) then reads the newest session with `getOAuthSessionForOrderAndEmail` and `continue`s whenever that session is younger than `SESSION_VALIDITY_HOURS` (48) and its status is neither `expired` nor `completed`, on the assumption that `pollOAuthSession` is still polling it. Nothing polls an order-scoped `failed` session: `pollOAuthSession` exits on `failed`, and `reconcileOAuthSessionsCron` filters `order_id IS NULL`. The mailbox is therefore not attempted again until the session crosses the 48-hour cutoff, at which point the loop's next branch marks it expired and retries. While retry-eligible failed inboxes remain the loop also never finalizes the order, so it stays in `requires_attention` with `completed_at` null; after 24 cycles `finalizeUnfulfillableOrderAfterRetries` stops retrying, and on the Autumn path that finalization releases the seats without refunding them.

## Blast radius

13 orders across 13 organizations, holding 95 mailboxes currently behind the gate (newest session `failed` and younger than the 48-hour cutoff), counted 2026-09-24T23:55Z with:

```
WITH latest AS (SELECT DISTINCT ON (order_id, email) order_id, email, status, created_at
  FROM cea_oauth_sessions WHERE order_id IS NOT NULL ORDER BY order_id, email, created_at DESC)
SELECT count(DISTINCT l.order_id), count(DISTINCT o.organization_id), count(*)
FROM latest l JOIN domain_purchase_order o ON o.id = l.order_id
WHERE l.status='failed' AND o.status='requires_attention' AND o.completed_at IS NULL
  AND l.created_at > now() - interval '48 hours'
```

One of the 13 has zero inboxes delivered; the other 12 are partially provisioned (3–24 inboxes) and cycling. Widening the query without the 48-hour condition returns 16 orders / 16 organizations / 125 mailboxes, but 6 of those hold newest failed sessions months old and are excluded from the retry loop by the latest-actionable-order filter, so they are not evidence for this gate. Memberships are single-user workspaces; distinct affected users were not counted separately.

## Proposed fix

Treat terminal session statuses as not in flight in the reconcile gate, so a mailbox whose connect failed is retried on the next pass, and give the connect step a bounded backoff for provider throttling so a 429 does not consume the mailbox's 24-attempt budget at a two-day cadence.

## What's included

The gate predicate and the retry cadence for order-scoped OAuth sessions. Not included: the separate reconnect paths that never resolve a provider mailbox id (ENG-13178), the stale `mail_domain` claim class (ENG-13213), and the Autumn decision about refunding seats that were never connected. ENG-14185's recorded "burning that budget over weeks" footprint is this gate's effect and should be cross-linked rather than merged.

## Regression seam

Reconcile pass over a `requires_attention` order whose mailbox's newest session is in `failed` status. Red before: no `retry-connect-oauth-` step runs and the inbox is untouched for the next 48 hours. Green after: the `failed` session does not block the pass and the attempted connect runs on that pass.

## Done when

* A mailbox whose newest session is `failed` is attempted again on the next reconcile pass instead of after 48 hours.
* A throttled connect does not consume one of the 24 retry attempts per two-day cycle.
* A regression test proves red-before/green-after at the seam above.

## Reports

* ENG-14249

relatedSnapshot.title: 14-Day Sending Block & Auto-Warmup Name 11
relatedSnapshot.description:
**Description:** **Context:** When users purchase "Non-Pre-Warmed" inboxes, there is a high risk they will immediately attach them to campaigns and burn the domains. We need to enforce a mandatory warmup period.

**Requirements:**

**1. The "Warmup Jail" (Sending Blocker):**

* **Logic:** For the first **14 Days** after creation, these inboxes must be **locked** from being assigned to any active *sending* campaigns.
* **UI:** Display a visible **"Warmup Countdown"** status next to the inbox (e.g., *"Warming Up: 13 Days remaining"*).
* **Override:** (Optional) Allow an "I understand the risk" manual override button, but buried behind a warning modal.

**2. Automatic Warmup Configuration:**

* **Action:** Upon provisioning, automatically trigger the Warmup API for these inboxes.
* **Settings:** Apply standard "Name 12" settings (e.g., Start with 2 emails/day, ramp up by 2/day, target 25-30).

**Goal:** Protect the user from their own impatience and ensure domains have high reputation before the first real campaign email goes out

relatedSnapshot.title: Customer report: 15 of 36 pre-warmed inboxes stuck in Error, Reconnect returns "Mailbox not found" and never clears the inbox
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Source

Intercom conversation: <url:app.intercom.com>

## Bounded conversation context

Customer reports (2026-09-21/22) that several mailboxes have shown an error and have not been sending for over a month; the count has grown from 6 to 15. He has opened several support tickets for the same issue over the past month or two without resolution. A frontline agent reactivated the inboxes on 2026-09-22 and it did not work. He asks for the 15 failing inboxes to be deleted and replaced with working ones and for one month of all 15 being down to be refunded / credited. Three screenshots of the Cold Email Agent email-accounts page were attached. Product area named on the conversation: Email accounts & domains.

## Testable claim

15 of the workspace's 36 pre-warmed sending inboxes are stuck in Error and have sent nothing because the Reconnect path asks the mail provider for a mailbox id it does not resolve, so the provider answers "Mailbox not found" and the inbox never returns to Active, leaving the workspace sending from only 21 inboxes.

## Current evidence

* Production: 33 mail_inbox rows for the workspace, 21 active/connected and 12 status=error, connected=false. The 12 carry three distinct connection errors: 6 "Mailbox OAuth connection threw an exception: Mailbox not found" with the stored provider id echoed in the message, 3 "Disconnected via Company One account_error webhook", 3 "Waiting on zapmail oauth connection".
* Provider: the workspace sub-workspace holds all 36 sending accounts; exactly 15 report a failed status with autofix_failed, timestamped between 2026-08-19 and 2026-09-21. Three of those 15 have no local mail_inbox row at all, which is why the local count reads 12 and the customer's count of 15 is the accurate one.
* OAuth session history for the workspace: 16 failed sessions, all "Mailbox OAuth connection threw an exception: Mailbox not found" between 2026-09-19 and 2026-09-22; 50 expired sessions, including repeated "Waiting on zapmail oauth connection" for three inboxes from 2026-08-19/20/21; 30 completed sessions earlier in 2026.
* Sending: the 21 healthy inboxes are still sending; a healthy inbox in the same workspace sent mail on 2026-09-22, the day of the report. An inbox in the failed group last sent on 2026-08-12.
* Name 13: failed process-account-error-reconnect runs in the last week, with the invoke-connect-oauth step failing.

## Suspected code path

* apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/campaign/workspaces/process-account-error-reconnect.ts (processAccountErrorReconnect) marks the inbox Error and invokes processConnectOAuth with mailboxId = the stored mail_inbox.provider_id.
* apps/web/trpc/routers/outreach/email-accounts.ts (triggerOAuthReconnect) sends mailboxId, orderId and domain as undefined for a customer-initiated Reconnect.
* apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/campaign/workspaces/process-connect-oauth.ts forwards that id to ColdMailReseller POST /mailboxes/oauth and records "Mailbox OAuth connection threw an exception: Mailbox not found. Context: mailboxId=<id>, email=<address>".
* apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/campaign/workspaces/poll-oauth-session.ts records "Waiting on zapmail oauth connection".

## Blast radius

Counted from production on 2026-09-24: 16,058 inboxes in Error across 1,167 organizations. Of those, 5,762 inboxes / 444 organizations carry the "Mailbox not found" reconnect error, 497 / 87 the account_error webhook state, and 339 / 174 the zapmail oauth class.

relatedSnapshot.title: When payment gives up, stop the plan, mailboxes and domains cleanly
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

ENG-8112 documented the original seven-day warning and auto-cancel decision. The operating model was revised on 11 September 2026 after measuring how billing actually works. Inboxes are charged monthly on each subscription's own anniversary and domains yearly, so there is no advance invoice 28 or 14 days before renewal. When a payment fails we warn the customer, let the provider's retries run, then switch provider renewal off so the inboxes expire at the end of the month we have already paid for, leaving a free reactivation window. This ticket owns production enforcement across payment events, base-plan/workspace termination, Zapmail, Company One, local state, recovery and audit evidence.

**Scope narrowed 29 Sep 2026.** This ticket now owns Flow B (the plan ends because the customer did not pay), Flow C (a mailbox payment fails while the plan is fine), the reactivation window and the provider-neutral design. Three parts moved out:

* the cancel steps themselves (renewal off at the supplier, per-domain resumable billing cancel) now live in ENG-14252;
* workspace and account deletion now lives in ENG-10782;
* the Autumn event classifier, the failure reason and the day 0, 3 and 7 warnings now live in ENG-13746.

Added: on Autumn, an expired plan never pauses campaigns today, because Autumn workspaces are always treated as protected. Autumn plans that expire must run the same pause and cleanup as Whop, and the automation switch (`SUBSCRIPTION_ACCESS_AUTOMATION_ENABLED`) is turned on after a dry-run review. Whether Acquisity/Acquisity#6288 is finished here or closed is an open question; recommended: close it and reuse the parts this ticket needs.

**Decided 29 Sep 2026:** no immediate cut-off. When billing stops (day 14, Stripe's final retry), supplier renewal is switched off and the mailboxes keep working until the month we have already paid the supplier for ends, then they are removed. We never cancel at the supplier early. The full timeline is on ENG-13358.

## Problem in plain English

When a mailbox payment fails, a base workspace plan is cancelled, or a workspace is deleted, customer access and Zapmail supplier billing can drift apart. Acquisity may stop collecting mailbox revenue while the Zapmail domain subscription remains live and billable.

A deletion can also remove the local records needed to find the supplier subscription later. One failed step can leave the mailbox active in Zapmail, connected in Company One, hidden locally, or some combination of those states.

## Confirmed production gap

The production Autumn webhook transport is configured and receiving signed events, but the current handler only acts on new, renew, upgrade and downgrade base-plan transitions. It accepts `past_due`, `expired` and `cancel` events with HTTP 200, marks them processed and performs no mailbox cancellation or reconciliation. Since 11 August, 947 `past_due` events for domain or inbox products across 113 billing accounts reached this path without triggering supplier cleanup.

This ticket must change that behavior. Relevant events must be classified and durably enqueued. They must not be acknowledged as successfully processed when the required state transition was skipped.

## Detailed behavior

### How renewal timing actually works (measured 11 September 2026)

* Each inbox subscription renews monthly on its own anniversary. The provider charges us about a day before it, and the customer's Autumn anniversary is effectively the same moment (median gap under an hour across a 1,800 domain sample).
* So a failed customer payment has always already cost us one provider month. Accept that month rather than moving billing anchors.
* About 12% of pre-warmed domains were registered as provider stock before a customer bought them, so their provider dates differ from the customer's. Every cutoff must use the provider period end, never the customer billing date.
* Domains are yearly and renew separately. Domain renewal is owned by ENG-13745.

### What cancel means (the same steps for every reason)

1. **Stop charging.** For a customer's own cancellation, stop at the end of the period they have paid for. For non-payment, stop immediately with no further retries.
2. **Switch provider renewal off for the inbox subscription.** The inboxes keep working until the end of the month already paid for, then expire. Never cancel immediately while a paid month is running.
3. **Reactivation window.** Until that provider month ends, a customer who pays or resubscribes gets everything back: renewal back on, billing re-attached, inboxes still warm.
4. **At the end of the provider month,** once the provider confirms the inboxes expired: remove them from sending (where sending is a separate provider), mark the domain and inboxes cancelled, email the customer, and switch domain renewal off so the domain is not renewed.
5. **Campaigns pause when the plan ends,** not when the inboxes expire. This is ENG-10751 behaviour extended to Autumn.

### Flow B: the plan ends because the customer did not pay

Day 0 is the failed payment.

* Days 0 to about 14: the warnings in ENG-13746 while Autumn retries the card.
* About day 14: the plan expires. Plan, inboxes and domains all cancel using the steps above and campaigns pause. Email: "Your plan has ended. Your inboxes will be removed on {provider month end} unless you reactivate."
* 3 days before removal: "Last chance to keep your inboxes."
* At removal: "Your inboxes and domains were removed."
* Payment recovered at any point before removal: everything is restored and the customer gets "Payment received, you're all set."

### Flow C: an inbox payment fails while the plan is fine

* The same as Flow B but scoped to that domain's inboxes.
* Day 0: alert and email, "Payment failed for 12 inboxes on <domain>", with the failure reason and how to fix it. Reminders on day 3 and day 7, and a final warning 2 days before the stop date, each repeating the reason (decided 29 Sep 2026).
* At Autumn expiry: stop billing and switch provider renewal off. Take those inboxes out of active campaigns so campaigns keep sending from the rest.
* Reactivation window until the provider month ends, then removal and an email.

### Works with any inbox provider

We plan to move inboxes to Company One. The timeline, reactivation window, emails and campaign pause live on our side, keyed to a generic provider period end. Each provider adapter supplies: read an inbox subscription's period end and renewal state; switch renewal on or off; renew or restore; confirm the inboxes ended; remove them from sending; list all inventory for the daily check. Where the provider and the sending platform are the same company, the remove-from-sending step is a no-op. Confirm how Company One bills us before writing that adapter.

### Also fix

A customer cancelling a single domain goes through the same steps, ending at the end of the paid period on both sides. Today the provider is cancelled immediately while Autumn bills to period end, so the customer loses service they have paid for.

### Durable renewal and cancellation workflow

Use an explicit resumable paid lifecycle:

`notice_scheduled → customer_charge_due → paid_for_next_period → supplier_renewal_due → supplier_renewal_verified → occurrence_completed → next_occurrence_scheduled`

After failed collection:

`cure_window → supplier_nonrenewal_requested → supplier_nonrenewal_verified → supplier_period_ended → full_domain_deletion_requested → full_domain_deleted → downstream_cleanup_pending → billing_reconciled → completed`

Each transition records attempts, timestamp, idempotency key, provider response summary and last error. A retry resumes at the first incomplete transition and cannot repeat completed external actions.

For a managed inbox domain, an inbox subscription still unpaid at the safe cutoff schedules supplier non-renewal while preserving the already-paid mailbox period. Only after that period ends and conclusive provider readback confirms service ended may Acquisity delete the full associated domain and every included inbox. Customer notices must explicitly explain this whole-domain consequence.

Terminal Zapmail deletion uses Cold Mail Reseller `DELETE /domains`, which deprovisions the domain, DNS, mailboxes and associated subscriptions. Provider contract correction, verified 9 September 2026: the CMR subscription event contract says the cancel endpoint takes effect immediately and deactivates mailbox accounts. It must not be treated as end-of-cycle nonrenewal or dispatched early while promising the funded period remains available. Disabling subscription auto-renew is a separate, documented operation (`POST /subscriptions/toggle-autorenewal`). Per the provider's documented lifecycle, renewal off means the subscription goes past due at period end, gets a 7 day grace period, then expires and the mailboxes are deactivated. Verify this once in the provider sandbox, including that the paid month keeps running and that switching renewal back on restores the mailboxes, before wiring the production flow. An accepted cancellation request is not proof of full-domain cleanup.

Before completing cancellation, calculate any remaining customer-funded annual-domain value and record the explicitly approved refund, credit or no-refund outcome on the renewal occurrence. Existing historical waste handled by ENG-13362 may still require immediate full-domain deletion after fresh evidence and explicit approval.

Supplier deletion is confirmed only by the required response and conclusive domain/subscription readback. Company One and local cleanup run only after the current supplier period ended and readback confirms service ended or the domain was deleted. A future non-renewal alone is not cleanup authorization. Downstream failures remain independently retryable and cannot restart supplier service, block cost prevention or repeat a destructive action.

### Workspace and account deletion

* Workspace, billing-account, order and mailbox deletion must not cascade away supplier identity or cancellation evidence.
* Trigger the same deprovisioning workflow before destructive deletion, or retain a tombstone until cleanup is complete.
* If safety requires blocking deletion until supplier cleanup succeeds, return a clear operator/customer error.
* Cover self-service, admin, bulk, script and framework deletion entry points that can affect the scoped inventory.

### Recovery, reversals and billing access

* Payment recovery before supplier non-renewal returns the occurrence to `paid_for_next_period`.
* Recovery after non-renewal was requested requires authoritative provider reconciliation. If cancellation cannot be reversed, either provision a new explicitly approved resource or refund/credit the customer; never claim the old resource was restored.
* Recovery after provider deletion requires new checkout or approved comp and never silently recreates infrastructure.
* A refund, dispute, chargeback or credit reversal before the supplier cutoff makes the future period uncovered and enters the cure/non-renewal path.
* If money is reversed after Acquisity paid the supplier, preserve live service for the funded supplier period, flag the contradiction, prevent the next renewal and apply the approved debt/refund/access policy.
* If the customer cancels after advance collection, refund only when supplier renewal can still be safely prevented. Otherwise preserve service for the funded period and schedule the following renewal off.
* If the customer paid but supplier renewal fails, enter supplier recovery and preserve entitlement plus Company One/local linkage. Complete only after readback proves restored service, or apply the defined refund/credit outcome if it cannot be restored.
* Ending the base workspace plan does not itself prove a separately paid or approved-free inbox subscription is unpaid. Evaluate each managed inbox domain against its own inbox entitlement and supplier period.
* Customers without an active base plan retain a billing-only route to view affected resources, warning, amount, payment recovery and cancellation deadline.

## Suggested implementation route

* Extend the signed Autumn event path and scheduled renewal backstop around the same durable renewal occurrence. Name 16 advance payment failure and recovery quickly; scheduled jobs own the reminder steps, the cutoff at the provider period end and the final provider readback. Provider calls stay outside the webhook request.
* Keep provider calls out of the webhook request. Persist the event idempotently, enqueue the durable workflow, and return success only after the required transition has been recorded.
* Route delinquency deadlines, base-plan termination and workspace deletion through one shared cancellation orchestrator.
* Build the state machine on durable records introduced by the entitlement ticket.
* Derive idempotency from the immutable entitlement plus cancellation occurrence, not from a domain name or scheduler run.
* Reuse the existing Cold Mail Reseller cancellation audit foundation where it satisfies these guarantees.
* Add operational alerts and an admin view for incomplete or repeatedly failing transitions.

## Done when

* the existing Autumn webhook no longer acknowledges and discards relevant `past_due`, `expired` or `cancel` events;
* tests prove the exact event scenarios above enqueue one idempotent transition and irrelevant products remain ignored;
* every cutoff is derived from the provider period end, and duplicate events cannot reset a deadline or the notification history;
* duplicate events cannot reset grace or duplicate cancellation;
* payment recovery before supplier cancellation stops pending removal;
* supplier, Company One, local and billing steps are resumable and individually auditable;
* base-plan cancellation and every workspace deletion path trigger the same guarantees;
* deletion cannot erase the evidence needed to finish cleanup;
* full-domain supplier deletion is verified against the exact domain, supplier subscription and included mailbox quantity;
* `/subscriptions/cancel` cannot be mistaken for completed full-domain offboarding;
* active campaigns are recorded and paused before Company One removal, while Company One or local failure cannot block or repeat confirmed Zapmail deletion;
* incomplete workflows alert with the failed transition, age and estimated monthly supplier cost;
* integration tests cover payment recovery before and after supplier cancellation, duplicate events, partial provider failure, workspace deletion with active mailboxes and retry from every transition.
* customer notices identify the full affected domain/inboxes, amount, charge date, cutoff and whole-domain deletion consequence;
* provider non-renewal preserves the already-paid period and never authorizes early Company One/local disconnection;
* an unpaid managed inbox-domain subscription can delete the full domain only after period-end readback and deterministic annual-domain refund/credit/no-refund handling;
* deadlines are derived from authoritative supplier timestamps and stored in UTC; missing or drifting dates become operator exceptions;
* changed quantity, price or renewal timestamp invalidates the stale occurrence before collection;
* paid customer/supplier renewal failure enters recovery and ends only in verified restored service or deterministic refund/credit;
* tests cover payment recovery racing the cutoff, duplicate scheduler/webhook delivery, provider timeout after non-renewal, and two workers claiming the same occurrence;
* the base-plan cascade runs: plan expiry cancels inboxes and domains through the same steps, and campaigns pause at plan expiry;
* Flow C removes only the unpaid domain's inboxes while other campaigns keep sending;
* paying inside the reactivation window restores everything with no new setup or provisioning;
* no provider inbox stays live with renewal on for a customer who is not paying, checked by the daily read.

## Blocked by

* ENG-14252, for the shared cancel steps.
* ENG-13746, for the event classifier and warnings.

Do not run this at the same time as ENG-11454: both add a "stop at plan end" step, and whichever lands second reuses the first.

## Implementation context

AI context.md

### Existing-inbox management implementation slice (9 September 2026)

After ENG-13526, James confirmed that Acquisity/Acquisity#6288 must provide one owner/admin link to see all existing inbox groups, including active paid, free and credit-funded groups, with actual customer prices and current service periods. Clients can keep all, cancel all, or keep some whole domain groups and cancel others. Choices and their consequences must be reviewed before confirmation.

Keeping a group must recover any exact existing invoice without duplicating it, repair future payment collection where needed, and establish or restore recurring billing for retained inboxes without purchasing or provisioning new ones. Paying an invoice alone is not completion. Show invoice liabilities separately from future monthly charges. Preserve paid siblings, allocate shared coverage once, and keep annual domain/platform rights separate. Cancellation must record and verify exact billing and supplier effects, preserve funded periods, and show requested, scheduled, pending and completed states honestly. Promises, internal budgets and reversals require their recorded decisions before any automatic demand.

This scope supersedes the earlier invoice-only and selection-only implementation limitation. It retains this ticket's existing ownership and broader lifecycle contract, and reuses ENG-13359 entitlement and ENG-13361 reconciliation work. Unsupported or ambiguous provider actions must have a specific guided resolution and must not be reported as completed.

Implementation, tests and the draft PR are authorized, including a dedicated access-protected preview using a separate synthetic database and Autumn/Stripe test credentials. Production issuance, notices, real charges/refunds, production subscription changes, supplier cancellations, rollout and merge are not authorized. Outreach sending remains dependent on a verified working flow. This slice does not mark the lifecycle programme or estate cleanup complete.

User problem summary:

The issues reported are:

* The campaign is expected to send 225 new emails per day across 15 email accounts, but only 195 emails per day are being sent, leaving a discrepancy of about 30 emails per day.

* The client needs confirmation on whether the platform supports this type of sequential sending behavior and whether the current setup could be affecting performance.
* The same slow campaign performance issue reportedly happened in a previous campaign, raising concerns about a recurring account-level or platform-level issue.
* The client is requesting:
  * investigation into the missing send volume,
  * explanation and resolution for the campaign stopping after May 6th,
  * clarification on sequence behavior/support,
  * review of historical account issues,
  * and guidance on whether reducing sequence complexity would improve performance.

relatedSnapshot.title: Stop one Outlook inbox from retrying forever on a permanently deleted email
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

One connected Outlook inbox has been stuck since last night in an endless retry loop and hasn't synced any new mail since. The cause is a single deleted email that Microsoft answers about in a way our sync doesn't expect, so it fails and immediately tries again, burning background-job time all day.

## Problem

When our Outlook sync notices an email has left a synced folder, it asks Microsoft whether that email simply moved to another synced folder or was actually deleted, before removing it from the CRM. For most deleted emails Microsoft plainly says "this doesn't exist anymore." For this particular email, Microsoft instead answers "access denied, wrong store ID" - a rarer response it sometimes gives for emails that were permanently purged. Our code doesn't recognize that answer as "the email is gone," so it treats it as an unexpected failure, retries several times over a few hours, gives up, and then starts over from scratch on the next sync trigger - forever, for that one inbox.

## Proposed fix

Teach the Outlook sync to also recognize this specific "access denied, wrong store ID" response as meaning the email is gone, the same way it already recognizes a plain "not found" response. Once recognized, sync treats the email as removed and moves on normally, and the affected inbox heals itself on its next sync run with no manual cleanup needed.

## What's included

* Recognizing this specific Microsoft Graph error shape (403 with this exact message) as "item no longer exists," alongside the existing "not found" (404) handling, in the two Outlook message-lookup helpers that can hit it.
* Not included: broader changes to Outlook sync retry behavior, concurrency, or reconnect handling - those are working as intended, and this is a narrow, one-error-shape fix.

## How it should work

* When Microsoft answers with this error while checking a deleted email's current location, sync treats it exactly like "not found": the email is not present in any synced folder, so it gets removed from the CRM (if it was ever imported) and the sync cursor advances normally.
* No change to how genuine access or credential problems are handled - those still stop sync and mark the account for reconnect.

## Who can do what

Not applicable: internal background sync behavior, no user-facing permissions change.

## What the user sees

No visible UI change. The practical effect: once deployed, the affected customer's Outlook inbox starts syncing new mail again on its next scheduled check, with no action needed from them or from us.

## Done when

* The two Outlook Graph message-lookup helpers treat this specific "access denied, wrong store ID" response the same as a "not found" response.
* The account behind ACQUISITY-558 completes a sync run successfully instead of failing.
* Automated tests cover this error shape.

## Open questions

None: all required decisions are settled.

## Expected outcome

Outlook sync stops retrying on permanently deleted emails that Microsoft reports this way, the currently stuck inbox recovers on its own, and background-job usage from this runaway loop stops.

## Implementation context

* Sentry issue: ACQUISITY-558 - 8K+ events over 20 hours, still escalating.
* Failing account: `calendarAccountId` `<uuid>`.
* Failing Graph call (from Sentry breadcrumbs): `GET /me/messages/{id}?$select=id,parentFolderId` returns HTTP 403, body "Access is denied. Check credentials and try again., The store ID provided isn't an ID of an item."
* Code to change: `apps/web/lib/integrations/email/outlook-api-client.ts` (`fetchOutlookMessage`, `fetchOutlookMessageParentFolderId`); add the classifier alongside `isOutlookSyncStateNotFoundError` in `apps/web/lib/integrations/email/outlook-graph-error.ts`.
* Confirmed not caused by the most recent Outlook PR (ENG-13963, merged 2026-09-21) - that PR left this code path byte-for-byte unchanged. The 404-only handling dates back to ENG-13962 (2026-09-19), when this sync path was first written.
